answer: Pair strangers for a live, branching exchange. They meet on shared ground, a knoll in the open, and must answer follow-ups that build on each other's last reply; every answer opens a new vertex the script did not foresee. A farm can mirror one script across many faces, but it cannot sustain dozens of distinct, adapting conversations at once. Copied replies contradict earlier turns, stall, or agree too perfectly, too fast — and the shared transcript exposes the mirror. Distinct minds diverge; copies betray themselves.
